questions.description: What does a singly linked list node contain?
questions.Option1: A value and an integer index into an array
questions.Option2: A stored value and a reference (pointer) to the next node
questions.Option4: A key and a hash code

questions.title: The Head Pointer
questions.description: Why is the head reference so important in a singly linked list?
questions.Option1: It is the only entry point — if you lose it, the whole list is unreachable
questions.Option2: It stores the largest value in the list
questions.Option3: It is a fixed-size array slot
questions.Option4: It always points to the last node

questions.Option1: The last node's next points to itself
questions.Option2: The last node stores the list length
questions.Option3: The last node's next is None
questions.Option4: There is no way to detect the end

questions.title: Head Insertion Cost
questions.description: Why is inserting a new node at the head of a linked list O(1)?
questions.Option1: Because every element shifts one position, like a Python list
questions.Option2: Because linked lists must be sorted first
questions.Option3: Because head insertion is O(n) in a linked list
questions.Option4: Because it only rewires the new node's next to the old head — no elements move

questions.title: Appending Without a Tail
questions.description: What does appending at the END cost in a singly linked list with no tail pointer?
questions.Option2: O(n) — you must walk the whole list to reach the last node

questions.title: List vs Linked List Access
questions.description: How do Python lists and linked lists compare for accessing the i-th element?
questions.Option1: A Python list reads index i in O(1); a linked list must traverse i nodes — O(n)
questions.Option2: A linked list reads index i in O(1)
questions.Option4: A Python list needs O(n) to read any element

questions.title: Snippet Chain Length
questions.description: What does this program print?
questions.codesnippet:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, val, nxt=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = nxt
head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
count = 0
n = head
while n:
    count += 1
    n = n.next
print(count)

questions.title: Snippet Insert Middle
questions.description: What does this program print?
questions.codesnippet:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, val, nxt=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = nxt
a, c = Node(1), Node(3)
a.next = c
b = Node(2)
b.next, a.next = a.next, b
n = a
while n:
    print(n.val)
    n = n.next

questions.title: Snippet Backwards Build
questions.description: Each value becomes the new head of a growing chain. What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
vals = [3, 7, 9]
prev = None
for v in vals:
    prev = [v, prev]
out = []
while prev:
    out.append(prev[0])
    prev = prev[1]
print(out)

questions.title: Iterative Reversal Result
questions.description: head is the chain 1 → 2 → 3. After this function runs, what does it return?
questions.codesnippet:
def reverse(head):
    prev = None
    cur = head
    while cur:
        nxt = cur.next
        cur.next = prev
        prev = cur
        cur = nxt
    return prev

questions.title: Snippet Middle Node
questions.description: head is the chain 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5. What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
slow = fast = head
while fast and fast.next:
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next.next
print(slow.val)

questions.title: Pointer Update Ordering Bug
questions.description: Inserting node B after node A in a singly linked list. What mistake loses part of the list?
questions.Option1: None — the order of the two assignments never matters
questions.Option2: Setting B.next corrupts the interpreter if done first
questions.Option3: Writing A.next = B before setting B.next = A.next — the rest of the chain is lost
questions.Option4: You must always delete the following node before inserting
